title: Same Monday
logline: Same architect, same Monday, stacked in split screen: on top she makes do with a plain generic version, below she has {{product.name}}. By 3pm only one of them is still winning, and the other one knows it.

lore: Brooks Studio is Nia's four-person architecture practice, three years old, on the second floor of a 1920s printing warehouse in Chicago. The floor still has bolt holes where the presses stood.
Today, Monday, at 3pm, she pitches a six-storey apartment building to the Ferrante family. The white foam model on the meeting table took the team eleven nights.
The little foam house on her desk is the first model she ever built, in her second year of college; its roof has been glued back on twice.
Her pencil cup is her grandfather's old blue coffee tin; it always holds six sharpened pencils and a soft drafting brush.
Both halves are the same room, the same objects, the same woman on the same Monday. Only one thing changes, the product she relies on, and with it the light, the mess and the stains.

world_bible.wear_and_time: One Monday, 9am to 3pm, lived twice in the same room with the same objects in the same places. The old way: warm tungsten, wrappers, crumbs, the rival's mess on the drafting pad, the pencil tin knocked over, a stained or rumpled cuff. The product way: cool window daylight, everything where it belongs, pencils upright in the tin, a clean cuff. The golden-hour pack shot at the end belongs to the product day.

the rival failing (a splat, a sputter, a zip splitting, a creak) against the product's clean sound
fingertips peeling off tacky laptop keys
pencils rolling out of the knocked-over tin
the soft creak of a woven-seat chair
the rival dropping into a wire bin with a hollow clank
street traffic hum through the tall window

rival.rule: The rival is a generic, unbranded version of the SAME product category as the product, in the same format and at the same scale, so the comparison is fair and specific. It is flat candy pink (flat dull beige if the product itself is pink), with no label, no text, no logo and no pattern, and never in the product's own colours. It never resembles a real competitor. Its flaws are small everyday annoyances, never health, safety or medical claims, and never a claim about any real brand.
rival.prop_prompt: Prop reference sheet on a plain mid-grey background, photoreal: one plain unbranded version of the product's category, the same format and size as the product, in a flat candy-pink colour with no label, no text, no logo and no pattern at all, slightly worn, with its archetype flaw visible (see by_archetype), shown front view and three-quarter view. Never red, blue or silver unless the product is pink. No letters, numbers or logos anywhere.

beats.summary: Split screen, both panes in sync: the same woman at 9am. Top: the pink rival fails on her. Bottom: the product works cleanly, she looks at us.
Ping-pong: 11am top, the rival's first annoyance; 11am bottom, fast clean sketching with the product; 3pm top, the rival's afternoon letdown at the meeting table.
3pm bottom: she presents the model, sharp and fast.
The split collapses, the product side takes the frame: the product at chest height, the product line.
The old-way Nia looks straight at her other self, concedes, and bins the rival.
The product beside the finished model at golden hour, tagline.
